title: Glaser replaces the band with Luis Russell's New York band
summary: At the Great White Way (formerly Connie's Inn) the union demanded standby men, so Glaser dropped Randolph's band and used Luis Russell's local New York band.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, I guess the record business was pretty bad at that time, and that's why there was no recording contract.
Is that the way it was?
Or was it just -- was Glaser Louis' manager by this time?

Yes, Glaser was still -- Glaser was still, because Glaser broke the band up, and, well, the reason why Glaser said, like I told you before, this is the band that Glaser sent back home because he took Louis Russell's band because he booked Louis in Great White Way. That used to be
Connie's Inn, and he said he wasn't going to pay that kind of money. They wanted him to hire the same number of men -- standby number of men that he had there.
Yeah. And so he said, I'm not going to do it. And so he took Louis Russell. Louis Russell was a New York local, and so he carried Louis Russell in there. And then Louis kept Louis Russell's band.
How long was the '34 band together?
Not too long, if I can remember. Because soon as we played -- I believe we did play South, though, I think we played the South, because we played New Orleans, too.
Where did you play in New Orleans, do you recall?

I think we played the South, because you know the -- oh, it's been so long (unintelligible) it's kind of getting a little hazy in my mind. But I know that we didn't stay together too long. I don't think.
